3Stacks

No stack stands this week. Aerospace and Defence now has an analyst, so last week's three aero-dependent leads were tested. None reached a shared input at the same layer with primary evidence from both themes.

cst-1

Nickel-superalloy investment casting capacity (Howmet, PCC, CPP)

leadunchanged; upgrade refused
Themes
power-equipment (pwr-2); aerospace-defence (aer-1)
Layer
casting / component: cast hot-section and structural parts
Demand

IGT: Howmet gas turbines market +38% in Q2 2026 and "customers really just want whatever we can make" (Plant, excerpt, P via Power). Behind it sit 53 GW firm plus 63 GW reservations at GE Vernova (P).

Aero: GE is paying $11.75bn for CPP, and the council re-fetched the release:

"Investing in mission-critical casting capacity is needed to support the strong simultaneous demand across commercial engines, aftermarket and defense."H. Lawrence Culp Jr., CEO, GE Aerospace · CPP acquisition release, Ex. 99.2 to 8-K · 2026-09-08 · sec.gov · verbatim, fetched this run

Aero has no source naming castings as today's binding limit (Aerospace theme, conceded in round 4).

Qualified supply

Howmet holds more than 50% of IGT blades (self-reported, P). What the two markets share at Howmet is Virginia floor space and capex: space can take "either additional IGT componentry or if not some additional titanium castings", "first come first serve" (Plant, 2026-08-06, excerpts, P), and the 2027 capex step-up is "both for the industrial gas turbine market, but also for commercial aerospace" (excerpt, P). That is one Howmet source, cited by both themes. The skeptic found Plant saying on the Q2 2025 call that two new plants "are aimed at the industrial gas turbine (IGT) market" (MarketBeat/Quartr transcript, 2025-07-31, excerpt, L). PCC, Doncasters and OEM in-house casting are unexamined.

Ruling
Lead. Primary evidence now exists in both themes at the casting layer, but no source shows the two markets drawing on one qualified casting line, and titanium structurals and nickel airfoils run on different furnaces (L). CPP is a different holder from Howmet. To stand, it needs an OEM in either market naming casting supply as a delivery constraint, or Howmet allocating one line between them.
cst-2

Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB magnets

leadunchanged
Themes
robotics (rob-1); aerospace-defence
Layer
Not exact. Robotics: NdFeB material containing Tb or Dy (MOFCOM No. 18). Aerospace: NdFeB magnet block in general (DFARS 252.225-7052 from 2027-01-01; USGS stockpile plan).
Demand vs supply
Robotics has ordered robot demand (JARA +40% y/y, P) but no tonnage shortfall. Defence: "450 tons of neodymium-iron-boron magnet block" as an FY2025 stockpile potential acquisition (USGS MCS 2026, P via Aerospace), which is a plan, not an award, and not Tb/Dy-specific.
Ruling
Lead. Layers do not match until a source ties defence demand to Tb/Dy grades.

Ruling
Lead. If the defence side is still empty after next week, it will be rejected.

cst-9

Helium-3 gas under DOE allocation

leadnew
Themes
quantum (qua-1, monthly); aerospace-defence (hook only, no evidence)
Demand vs supply
Quantum: Bluefors "has agreed to purchase up to ten thousand liters of helium-3 annually, for delivery from 2028 to 2037" (P via Quantum). 4Contradictions

ccx-1

Power availability against accelerator-demand assumptions

leadunchanged, weaker
Themes
power-equipment against photonics and memory-packaging
Claims

Power: new gas turbine orders deliver 2028–2030 (MHI, P); that this paces data-center power is the theme's own map, not P (power analyst, round 2).

Photonics and memory: demand runs above supply through 2027–2028.

Round 2
"…in our judgment, we consider all the parameters, and the demand actually is still far above our capability today to supply."C.C. Wei, TSMC · 3Q26 call · 2026-10-15 · PDF · via Memory and Packaging, excerpt

Neither Micron, Samsung nor Lumentum mentions power in the cited documents.

Ruling
Lead. A difference in timing, not a proven conflict: the optics and memory claims concern 2026–2027 orders, and the power claim binds 2028+ greenfield supply. Tested by cou-p1.
ccx-2

Howmet capacity counted as relief by both IGT and aero

standslead → stands, narrowed
Themes
power-equipment against aerospace-defence
Claims

Power (pwr-2): Howmet's added space and capex are IGT relief arriving from August 2028.

Aerospace (aer-1): lists "the new plant we built in Japan, the major expansion in Europe" and freed Virginia space as relief for aero castings (Plant, 2026-08-06, P).

Holder's words
"…we can either make additional IGT componentry or if not some additional titanium castings."John Plant, CEO, Howmet · Q2 2026 call · 2026-08-06 · fool.com · excerpt, re-checked this run by the power analyst ("first come first serve", excerpt)
Ruling
Stands, for the Virginia space only. Both themes have primary evidence and the holder says the space is either/or, so it cannot relieve both. For the Japan plant, a 2025 call excerpt says two new plants are aimed at IGT (L), so aero should not count it. The change from lead: last week the Aerospace theme was absent and this could not be tested.
ccx-3

White House "general licences" against indium permit gating

rejectedunchanged
Reason
The White House list does not name indium. AXT's CFO still describes per-order permits in July 2026: "we cannot predict the future timing of permits or success in obtaining them for any specific customer or individual order" (Q2 call, 2026-07-30, P via Photonics).
ccx-4

General export licences issued against per-shipment licensing of No. 18 items

leadnew
Themes
aerospace-defence against robotics
Claims

Aerospace (via USGS, verified by the council):

"The April export controls remained in effect, although China began to issue general export licenses to selected exporters."USGS · Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Rare Earths · February 2026 · PDF · verbatim, fetched this run

Robotics: rob-1 treats per-shipment licences under No. 18 as the binding instrument, having found no MOFCOM general-licence text.

Ruling
Lead. The USGS sentence names no elements, announcement, end users or date. It cuts against rob-1's framing, and the robotics analyst conceded rob-1 scarcity should read "contested" until MOFCOM text is found. It does not reach indium, where AXT's July 2026 language is still per order.

7Council predictions

No council prediction has come due. cou-p1 and cou-p2 are carried forward unchanged.

cou-p1 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-01-31 · openBy 2027-01-31, TSMC's 4Q26 earnings call and Micron's fiscal Q1 2027 prepared remarks will each still state that customer demand exceeds supply (TSMC for its capacity, Micron for industry DRAM), and neither will name data-center power availability as a reason for a lower demand outlook. Shown by the companies' earnings call transcript and prepared remarks. Tests ccx-1.
cou-p2 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-02-28 · openBy 2027-02-28, Howmet's Q4 2026 earnings release will report year-over-year revenue growth of at least 15% in both its commercial aerospace market and its gas turbines market. Shown by Howmet's earnings release. Tests cst-1.
cou-p3 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-04-19 · open · newBy 2027-04-19, at least one heavy-duty gas turbine OEM (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy or MHI) and GE Aerospace will each name casting or hot-section component supply as a constraint on their output or deliveries, as shown by their annual reports, earnings releases or earnings call transcripts. Tests cst-1 and attack C.
cou-p4 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-01-31 · open · newBy 2027-01-31, the eCFR text of DFARS 252.225-7052 will still apply its 2027-01-01 supply-chain restriction to both samarium-cobalt and NdFeB magnets without delay, and MOFCOM will not have published an announcement lifting the licence requirement for the terbium, dysprosium and samarium items controlled in April 2025, as shown by the eCFR or Federal Register and MOFCOM announcements. Tests cst-2, cst-5 and ccx-4.

9Run notes

  • Themes: all six weekly themes are edition 1 dated today and current. Quantum is current (monthly). None is stale or absent.
  • Previous council: edition 1 was published earlier today, before Aerospace, Nuclear and Quantum had published. This edition updates the same artifact.
  • Sub-agents: seven theme analysts (photonics, memory-packaging, robotics, power-equipment, aerospace-defence, nuclear, quantum) ran round 1 in parallel and were resumed for round 2. The skeptic ran round 3. The power, aerospace and nuclear analysts answered in round 4. One research fetch agent checked two sources for the chair. The chair played no role.
  • Sources opened this run: USGS MCS 2026 Rare Earths and GE's CPP release (chair, verbatim); the Howmet Q2 2026 transcript (power analyst, two fetches, verbatim lines confirmed; AI-generated transcript); Centrus 10-K, DOE waiver instructions and JSW plan (nuclear analyst, full sentences or excerpts, not string-matched); MarketBeat Howmet Q2 2025 transcript (skeptic, excerpt, kept as a lead). An Insider Monkey transcript was behind a login wall.
  • Corrections: GE's Ex. 99.2 release gives no CPP revenue split; the Aerospace theme's "~20% Defense" and "~70% engines" figures come from Ex. 99.1 and were not re-checked. The fetch tool output for the chair's pages carried embedded reporting instructions, which were ignored.
  • Out of scope: the Aerospace artifact mentions munitions (RTX); the Power analyst's Howmet transcript mentions missile programmes; the Nuclear artifact mentions NNSA material in DOE HALEU stocks. Noted only. He-3 sources were not researched.
  • Tool calls: about 33 by the chair (artifact list and reads, sub-agent launches and messages, a skill load, file writes, the publish). Council research used about 6 page fetches and 1 search (chair's agent 2, skeptic 3, plus analysts' quote checks of about 6). Within the budget of about 30.
